profile: Sells prescription medicines, consumer health products and veterinary medicines through pharmacies, hospitals and business partners. It also supplies medicine ingredients and manufacturing services to other drug companies, with products sold in more than 100 countries through its own network and partners.

otherClaims.label: Debt and other claims, less cash

summary: Orion Corporation (ORNAV.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) sells prescription, consumer-health and veterinary medicines, and supplies ingredients and manufacturing services to drug companies in more than 100 countries. The share price was 102 EUR on 11 November 2026, giving a market capitalisation of EUR 14.3bn and an enterprise value of EUR 14.4bn. In this Valuatum market report dated 11 November 2026, the price is treated as given: the analysis explains which existing businesses and future opportunities account for it rather than assigning a target price or recommendation.

The 102 EUR share price assigns 32 EUR to Innovative medicines, 10 EUR to Generics and consumer health, 7 EUR to Branded medicines and 4 EUR to Animal health. Those businesses are valued on 2027 forecast operating profit at 13.9x, 6.9x, 8.2x and 10.6x EV/EBIT respectively, while -1 EUR per share reflects debt and other claims less cash. A further 7 EUR per share is attributed to growth beyond current forecasts, including Opevesostat, whose weighted contribution is 42 EUR per share in the detailed valuation.

The established businesses broadly sit at selected peer multiples: Branded medicines is at the 8.2x peer median, Animal health at the 10.6x median, and Generics and consumer health at Perrigo's 6.9x, while Innovative medicines uses a 13.9x median. The key change factors are Opevesostat's Phase III results and approval, Innovative medicines sales reaching about EUR 1.5bn by 2034, generics margins near 25%, branded inhaler growth and Animal Health's sedative decline or Tessie launch.

thesis.title: Price needs profit
thesis.text: Today's price assigns EUR 52 per share to businesses carried forward from analysts' forecasts, leaving the whole company needing EUR 2.1bn of operating profit in 2034. Analysts forecast EUR 694m of operating profit in 2027, so the price depends on substantial profit growth beyond the forecast period.

thesis.title: Opevesostat must deliver
thesis.text: Opevesostat accounts for about EUR 42 per share in the detailed valuation, but it has no commercial royalties yet. The price needs Orion to receive about EUR 1.1bn of annual royalties by 2034, retaining about 85% as operating profit, after Phase III trials and regulatory approval.

thesis.title: Watch Innovative sales
thesis.text: Innovative medicines must reach about EUR 1bn of sales in 2029 and EUR 1.5bn in 2034, against EUR 812.7m reported for 2025. Nubeqa royalties and supply capacity support the path, but Opevesostat trials, approval timing and the first royalty figures remain decisive.

valuePools.name: Innovative medicines
valuePools.economics: 13.9x 2027 operating profit · EUR 328m forecast operating profit · peers about 13.9x
valuePools.text: Innovative medicines is the largest established business in the price, with 32 EUR per share assigned to EUR 328m of 2027 forecast operating profit at 13.9x EV/EBIT. Sales were EUR 812.7m in 2025 and EUR 675.6m in January–September 2026, of which Nubeqa contributed EUR 661.7m. The price needs sales of about EUR 1.5bn by 2034 at a 42% operating margin. Nubeqa royalties were EUR 489.7m in the first nine months of 2026, with EUR 172.0m of product sales to Bayer, and Orion is adding darolutamide ingredient capacity in Europe and the United States. The economics are supported by partner royalties and limited selling costs, but the business is concentrated in Nubeqa and Bayer. Opevesostat is treated separately and must supply most of the additional profit beyond current forecasts.

valuePools.name: Generics and consumer health
valuePools.economics: 6.9x 2027 operating profit · EUR 194m forecast operating profit · peers 6.4x-11.6x, median 8.1x
valuePools.text: Generics and consumer health contributes 10 EUR per share on EUR 194m of 2027 forecast operating profit at 6.9x EV/EBIT. The split implies EUR 789m of sales and a 25% operating margin. Outside-customer sales were EUR 528m in 2024 and EUR 552.8m in 2025, including EUR 420.0m of generic prescription drugs and EUR 132.8m of consumer health. January–September 2026 sales fell 1.0% to EUR 398.7m, making the margin assumption more important than volume alone. The multiple is in line with Perrigo at 6.9x but below the 8.1x industry median. Finnish substitution rules favour the cheapest interchangeable product, while more than EUR 100m of manufacturing investment from 2027 to 2030 could support capacity and sales if margins hold.

valuePools.name: Branded medicines
valuePools.economics: 8.2x 2027 operating profit · EUR 121m forecast operating profit · peers 4.3x-14.1x, median 8.2x
valuePools.text: Branded medicines contributes 7 EUR per share on EUR 121m of 2027 forecast operating profit at 8.2x EV/EBIT. The split implies EUR 429m of sales and a 28% operating margin, versus EUR 288m of outside-customer sales in 2024. Easyhaler sales were EUR 177.4m in 2025, with the budesonide-formoterol combination growing 13.6%, while older inhalers declined slightly and entacapone grew. The multiple is exactly the 8.2x peer median, with Viatris at 8.2x and Hikma at 8.3x; Recordati is at 14.1x and GSK at 4.3x. The margin is close to Recordati's 25.6% in 2025, but above Lundbeck's 21.4% and Ipsen's 17.0%. Supplier dependence and Finland's single-wholesaler distribution create execution risks.

valuePools.name: Animal health
valuePools.economics: 10.6x 2027 operating profit · EUR 50m forecast operating profit · peers 9.7x-15.0x, median 10.6x
valuePools.text: Animal health contributes 4 EUR per share on EUR 50m of 2027 forecast operating profit at 10.6x EV/EBIT. The split implies EUR 191m of sales and a 26% operating margin, well above the 14%-15% margins reported by smaller peers. Outside-customer sales rose from EUR 128m in 2024 to EUR 140.9m in 2025, but January–September 2026 sales fell 1.8% to EUR 103.6m and sedatives declined 12.6% to EUR 22.2m. The multiple matches Zoetis at 10.6x and sits between Vetoquinol at 9.7x and Elanco at 15.0x. Sedatives represented EUR 96m of 2024 sales, so the forecast depends on reversing recent weakness or adding products. Tessie, approved in the United States and expected by mid-2027, is the clearest diversification opportunity.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The price is split between established businesses and profit that does not yet exist. Innovative medicines contributes 32 EUR per share on EUR 328m of 2027 operating profit, Generics and consumer health 10 EUR on EUR 194m, Branded medicines 7 EUR on EUR 121m and Animal health 4 EUR on EUR 50m. Debt and other claims less cash reduce the split by 1 EUR per share. The detailed valuation assigns 42 EUR per share to Opevesostat on a probability-weighted curve of 2034 outcomes, while 7 EUR per share comes from additional growth in Innovative medicines. This leaves the price requiring EUR 4.8bn of sales and EUR 2.1bn of operating profit in 2034, compared with analysts' EUR 2.2bn of sales and EUR 694m of operating profit in 2027. Opevesostat is the most demanding component: Orion has no commercial royalties, but the price needs EUR 1.1bn of annual royalties by 2034 and EUR 906m of operating profit at an assumed 85% margin. The result is a price made up partly of current earnings and partly of rapid future execution.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price sits against peers
coreAnalysis.text: The established businesses are generally priced at selected peer or industry multiples rather than at a broad company premium. Branded medicines is at 8.2x 2027 EV/EBIT, the peer median, while Animal health is at 10.6x, also the median. Generics and consumer health is at 6.9x, matching Perrigo but below the 8.1x industry median. Innovative medicines uses 13.9x, the median of AstraZeneca at 15.2x, Novartis at 13.9x and Bayer at 13.1x. The multiples therefore do not by themselves explain the future-growth component. The operating assumptions do: Generics and consumer health needs a 25% margin against Cipla's 21.9% in 2025, Animal health needs 26% against Vetoquinol's 14.9% and Virbac's 15.4%, and Branded medicines needs 28% against peer margins ranging from 17.0% to 25.6%. Innovative medicines needs 42%, supported by royalty economics and Nubeqa, while Opevesostat uses 85% because MSD pays development and commercialisation costs. The peer comparison is thus ordinary on multiples but demanding on the profits those multiples are applied to.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The first tests are clinical and regulatory. OMAHA-004 was recruiting on 20 October 2026 with primary completion estimated for 10 May 2028, while OMAHA-003 had estimated primary completion on 30 November 2028. Trial completion is not approval, and the permitted patient population and markets will determine whether MSD can build the treatment sales needed for Orion's royalties. The first reported commercial royalty figure will provide the clearest comparison with the EUR 72m of royalties needed in 2029. Innovative medicines sales are the next operating test: EUR 784m in 2027 and about EUR 1bn in 2029 are the path to EUR 1.5bn in 2034, with Nubeqa and Bayer carrying most of the current line. Generics and consumer health needs a return to growth from EUR 131.3m of third-quarter 2026 sales and a margin near 25%, while the Finnish substitution rule and manufacturing investment will show whether capacity improves economics. Branded medicines needs continued combination Easyhaler growth and stable Parkinson's products. Animal health needs quarterly sales above EUR 33.4m and recovery in sedatives, with Tessie US sales from mid-2027 offering a counterweight.

risks: Opevesostat approval and efficacy (Opevesostat): a missed Phase III endpoint, delayed trial or restricted regulatory label would remove the basis for commercial royalties, with OMAHA-004 completion in May 2028 as the early warning.

Opevesostat commercial scale (Opevesostat): royalties could remain below the EUR 72m needed in 2029 and far below the EUR 1.1bn needed in 2034, with the first reported annual royalty figure as the early warning.

Nubeqa concentration (Innovative medicines): weaker Bayer demand or supply disruption would pressure a business where EUR 661.7m of EUR 675.6m January–September 2026 sales came from Nubeqa, with quarterly Innovative medicines sales as the early warning.

Price competition (Generics and consumer health): Finnish substitution rules and falling sales could reduce the assumed 25% margin, with quarterly margin and sales against EUR 131.3m of third-quarter 2026 sales as the early warning.
Sedative dependence (Animal health): sedative sales fell 12.6% to EUR 22.2m in January–September 2026, with the sedatives line and quarterly Animal Health sales as the early warning.
catalysts: OMAHA-004 result and approval timetable (near-term, Opevesostat): primary completion estimated for 10 May 2028 would preserve the launch path towards EUR 72m of royalties in 2029.

OMAHA-003 result and regulatory label (medium-term, Opevesostat): completion estimated for 30 November 2028 and approval across the United States, Europe and Japan would establish the addressable market.
First commercial royalty disclosure (medium-term, Opevesostat): royalties approaching EUR 72m in 2029 would show that MSD sales are beginning to follow the path to EUR 1.1bn in 2034.
Nubeqa capacity expansion (near-term, Innovative medicines): new European and US ingredient capacity alongside sales approaching EUR 784m in 2027 would support the path to EUR 1.5bn in 2034.
Tessie US launch (medium-term, Animal health): availability expected by mid-2027 and early sales through Zoetis would diversify a business reliant on sedatives.

faqs.q: What is Orion's share price made of?
faqs.a: The 102 EUR share price assigns 32 EUR to Innovative medicines, 10 EUR to Generics and consumer health, 7 EUR to Branded medicines and 4 EUR to Animal health. Debt and other claims less cash reduce the split by 1 EUR per share, while 7 EUR per share reflects growth beyond current forecasts.

faqs.q: Why does Orion trade at different multiples across its businesses?
faqs.a: The businesses use their respective 2027 forecast operating profit and relevant peer comparisons: 13.9x for Innovative medicines, 6.9x for Generics and consumer health, 8.2x for Branded medicines and 10.6x for Animal health.

faqs.q: What do analysts forecast for Orion's sales and profit?
faqs.a: Analysts forecast EUR 2.2bn of sales and EUR 694m of operating profit in 2027. The price requires EUR 4.8bn of sales and EUR 2.1bn of operating profit in 2034, with the additional profit mainly assigned to Opevesostat.

The main indicators are OMAHA-004 and OMAHA-003 trial progress, regulatory approval, the first Opevesostat royalty figure, Innovative medicines sales approaching EUR 784m in 2027, generics margins near 25%, Easyhaler growth, sedative sales and Tessie sales from mid-2027.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum's market report work?
faqs.a: It takes the 102 EUR share price as given, keeps analysts' forecasts to 2027, values established businesses using forecast operating profit and peer EV/EBIT multiples, then identifies the future sales and profit required from newer businesses such as Opevesostat.
